description:
Each publication consumer keeps one test that it goes through the shared publication mechanism, in place of a copy of the mechanism's crash matrix.

## Background

The project requires a mechanism's behaviour matrix to be proven once against the mechanism, with each consumer proving only that it reaches it. Publication violates that in four places. A profile-lifecycle suite drives the whole failure-point set through `profile apply` and classifies it with a compile-enforced thirty-six-arm match. A gate-durability test, two linked-checkout write-policy tests, and two recover-command tests each re-inject a commit-decision or prepared-state failure to restate the same convergence property.

The record's own conformance suite already owns the matrix and restores compile-enforced coverage of the point set, so the consumer copies have an owner to defer to. This is also the largest single-file reduction available outside the kernel.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The profile-lifecycle interruption suite no longer enumerates a publication failure-point set, and `profile apply` retains one test asserting that it publishes through the shared session.
- [hard] REQ-02: Gate evaluation retains one test asserting that a gate run's durable evidence is coupled to the issue change.
- [hard] REQ-03: The linked-checkout write-policy suite retains its policy coverage, with publication convergence left to the mechanism's suite.
- [hard] REQ-04: The recover command's suite retains its command-contract tests, with journal-shaped prepared state left out.
- [hard] REQ-05: No exhaustive classification of a publication failure-point set survives outside the mechanism's own suite.
- [hard] REQ-06: The change removes more test lines than it adds.

## Notes

Stale-capture rejection under concurrent profile application is a separate property with its own suite and survives untouched here.
title: Consumer-side publication matrix retirement
